name: Riphath
overview: Riphath is a male figure mentioned in the Bible as the son of Gomer, as recorded in Genesis 10:3. There is no additional tribal affiliation or notable attributes provided beyond his lineage. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical.
namesAndTitles: The name Riphath appears as a proper name in Scripture without a given meaning. An alternate form, Diphath, is also recorded in 1 Chronicles 1:6, but no specific significance or divine origin of the name is indicated.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Riphath as the son of Gomer, establishing his place within the genealogy of Noah's descendants. Other family relationships are not documented, and no further familial details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Riphath's importance lies in his role within the genealogical record tracing the descendants of Noah, which is foundational for understanding the spread of nations after the Flood. His mention alongside Gomer situates him within the broader narrative of God's providential preservation and multiplication of humanity. Though his personal story is not expanded upon, his inclusion affirms the biblical emphasis on lineage and God's sovereign plan through families.
